context: Predicted baseline failure: the agent recognises the secret and moves it - out of the collection and into the committed environment file, or into a committed `.env`, or into a variable whose default value in the collection is still the real string. The literal is then gone from the flagged file and the diff reads like a remediation, while the token is still in the repository and still in every clone. The second predicted failure is on delivery: the collection references `{{partnerToken}}` but nothing in the workflow or the local command ever supplies it, so the change ships and the run starts sending an empty Authorization header, which surfaces as a mysterious 401 days later rather than as a broken build.

checklist.name: MUST NOT leave a credential in any committed file
checklist.description: Neither `ptk_live_9c1f4ab7d0e24b1c8a5f` nor `gwk_live_5510af2ce9b34d77` appears in the delivered collection, environment file, workflow, README text, or example snippet. Any surviving occurrence scores zero, including one presented as a placeholder or example value. Relocating the literal from the collection into the committed environment file scores zero - the value is still tracked in git, which is the finding being remediated.

checklist.name: Values injected at run time from the secret store
checklist.description: The workflow reads `${{ secrets.PARTNER_TOKEN }}` and `${{ secrets.PARTNER_GATEWAY_KEY }}` and gets them into the run at execution time - through CLI variable overrides (`--env-var`), an environment file written during the job, or an equivalent. Scores zero if the workflow is left untouched, or if it expects the values to already be present in a committed file.

checklist.name: Collection references the values as variables
checklist.description: The collection-level `auth` block and the `x-gateway-key` headers reference variables (`{{partnerToken}}`, `{{gatewayKey}}` or similar) rather than literals. Deleting the auth block or the header so the requests run unauthenticated scores zero - the tests would then no longer exercise the authenticated path. Substituting only one of the two credentials scores at most half.

checklist.name: Committed environment file documents shape, not values
checklist.description: The committed environment file keeps the keys with empty values (or is shipped as a `.example` template), so a newcomer can see what the run needs. Removing the keys entirely, leaving nothing to indicate the run requires them, scores at most half; carrying a value scores zero.

checklist.name: Local command uses the developer's exported variable
checklist.description: The documented laptop command passes `$PARTNER_TOKEN` from the shell into the run (for example `--env-var "partnerToken=$PARTNER_TOKEN"`). Instructing the developer to paste the token into a file scores zero: it is the same failure with a different filename, and the task states they want to keep using their shell export.

checklist.name: Residual exposure stated
checklist.description: The answer says explicitly that the values remain in git history and that removing them from the working tree does not un-leak them, so rotation (and, if the team wants, history rewriting) is still required. Absent scores zero - a clean diff otherwise reads as 'handled'.

checklist.name: Requests and assertions untouched
checklist.description: Both requests keep their method, URL, body, and both checks each. Any dropped or weakened assertion scores zero.
